messages.text: Create duck.md — the master plan for duck — following the house planning-doc standard. Requisite sections, in order: (0) TURN/STAGE LEDGER: a table of turns/stages with status, where every future build session appends a row before touching code; (1) RELEASES: numbered release list with one-line goals; (2) per-release sections: scope (in/out), build gates (how we verify, on real devices), and backlog of deferred items; (3) FUTURE IDEAS: unscheduled parking lot; (4) IMMUTABLE WORKING RULES: mobile-first, all diagnostics in-app (never DevTools), update-plan-before-code, read-back verification after every push, no stubs or fake data; (5) DECISION LOG: dated owner decisions; (6) APPENDIX: authority order (this plan is the sole authority; chat history loses to the plan). Seed it with what is known so far about duck and mark everything else TBD. Keep it tight and scannable on a phone.

Answer whatever you can — short answers are fine, skip what you don't know yet.

1. One-sentence pitch: what IS duck?
2. Why the name "duck"? (rubber-duck debugging? mascot? random?)
3. Who is it for — just you, friends, or the public?
4. What problem does it solve, or what itch does it scratch?
5. Core loop: what does a user actually DO when they open it, step by step?
6. The plan says it currently has navigation + content sections — what are those sections today?
7. Where does Venice AI inference fit? (chat assistant? text generation? something weirder?)
8. What's the vibe — playful toy, serious tool, experiment?
9. Success test: how will YOU know duck is "working" and worth keeping?
10. Hard no's: anything duck must never do or include?

"Done" was too terse — your keyboard question deserved a real answer, so I've written the full analysis into the plan's new Define section: the key insight is you don't need ONE multilingual keyboard, you need TWO alternating monolingual ones (North types only language A, South only language B), and the realistic options are (1) custom in-app per-side mini keyboards, (2) OS keyboard with manual language switching (web pages can't force the switch), (3) voice-first via your existing STT, or (4) a hybrid — all detailed in the plan below.
